structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Record $230.4B backlog and large Missiles and Fire Control backlog expansion are consistent with constrained defense-production demand, including PAC-3/THAAD and other munitions ramps.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Demand spans air/missile defense, tactical missiles, combat aircraft, undersea systems and strategic/space programs rather than one end market.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Mission integration, installed programs and qualification barriers create friction, but budget reprioritization, competing platforms and alternate suppliers can shift future awards.

structural-causal.name: supplyChainResilience
structural-causal.basis: Production ramps demonstrate capacity expansion, while specialized components and ramp execution remain explicit constraints.

discovery-weak-signals.name: missile production framework
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Production acceleration supports long-duration air-dominance demand visibility.

adversarial-red-team.name: thesisQuality
adversarial-red-team.basis: Strategic demand and backlog are well supported, but economics remain exposed to program accounting, contract structure and execution.

adversarial-red-team.name: financialOperatingMomentum
adversarial-red-team.basis: Sales grew 11% and guidance rose, while profit comparability is flattered by prior-year reach-forward losses and cash flow benefited from receipt timing.

adversarial-red-team.name: pricingPower
adversarial-red-team.basis: High demand does not imply unrestricted pricing because government procurement and contract structures constrain economics.

expectations-execution.name: execution visibility
expectations-execution.basis: A production-acceleration framework is stronger than roadmap-only demand.

items.risk: Funding, award structure, supply chain and ramp execution can limit realized economics.
Program charges and supply-chain constraints can impair conversion of demand into cash flow.
Successor bottlenecks are specialized supply availability, funded contract structure and production-ramp execution rather than demand alone.
Government/allied concentration makes budget, authorization and export decisions structurally important to conversion timing.
Backlog can overstate near-term economic realization when funding, definitization, delivery schedules or working capital delay conversion.
Fixed-price and complex development programs can generate reach-forward losses even in a strong demand environment; 2025 included $1.6B of such program losses.
Customer concentration in governments and allies creates budget, political, export and procurement exposure.
Specialized supply-chain and ramp constraints can prevent strategic demand from becoming deliveries on expected timing.

contradictions.claimA: Record backlog and production ramps support long-duration demand visibility.
contradictions.claimB: Cash conversion and program economics have shown material timing and execution volatility.
contradictions.disposition: Both can be true; demand visibility is structural evidence, while realized economics remain execution-dependent and should not be inferred from backlog alone.

contradictions.claimA: Q2 2026 operating profit increased sharply year over year.
contradictions.claimB: A large portion of the comparison reflects $1.6B of prior-year reach-forward losses rather than solely current-period productivity.
contradictions.disposition: Resolved as a comparability issue, not a blocker; retain underlying sales/ramp evidence separately from year-over-year profit optics.

contradictions.claimB: Company disclosure attributes much of the increase to customer-receipt timing and lower tax payments.
contradictions.disposition: Resolved as timing sensitivity; use multi-period cash conversion rather than extrapolating the quarter.
